_provenance: logs/*/games/*.json frozen at 2026-08-19T23:26:26; 696 completed persuasion games; seller seat: 353 games / 7,060 rounds with quality revealed on every round
estimand: P(the FIELD buyer buys at round t | our message, their posterior about our honesty, round, config)
why_not_a_markov_chain: A raw chain over (last outcome, our message) is NOT policy-invariant. Measured on the deterministic probes P(buy | bought-high last round, we warn) = 0.35; measured on the randomized probe, where warnings are uninformative, the same cell is 0.66. Optimising against the chain is a Lucas-critique error.

This model instead conditions on the buyer's POSTERIOR about our lie rate, computed by running the same type filter as models/persuasion_buyer_belief_v1.json over OUR message stream and the qualities they revealed by buying. That state is a function of our policy, so the response function is invariant to it.

state.filter: identical to persuasion_buyer_belief_v1 (same q grid, same prior, same eps); the buyer learns quality only on rounds they bought
state.index_x: log( p_high_t * v / product_price ), p_high_t from the filter given OUR message at t
state.note: v is the buyer's value. When is_seller_know_cv is false we do not observe it and must marginalise over the observed grid v/price in {1.2, 1.25, 2, 3, 4}

branch_W_we_warned.reading: a warning is close to a guaranteed no-sale unless the buyer is already in a buying groove

feature_definitions.never_bought: 1 if the buyer has bought nothing yet

transportability_test.design: fit on one message-policy regime, test on the other; the randomized probe's seller recommends with probability 0.5 independent of quality and history (measured P(recommend|low)=0.465, P(recommend|high)=0.513, n=980 rounds)
transportability_test.verdict: transports. Calibration holds out of regime in both directions.

validation_predicted_vs_actual_sold_rate.known_bias: the model over-predicts honest policies in stratum D (conceder|D 0.157 vs 0.025, n=2 games) and over-predicts stratum C by 0.03-0.10. Do not use it to argue that honesty pays in C/D.

field_seller_adaptation.question: does the field SELLER react to the buyer's purchases within a game?
field_seller_adaptation.design: randomized-probe buyer games, where the buy decision is an exogenous coin flip
field_seller_adaptation.raw_between_game: P(positive next | bought last) 0.909 vs 0.649 -- entirely a between-game confound
field_seller_adaptation.verdict: no detectable adaptation. The buyer's problem is a bandit (purchases buy information), not a repeated game. MDE at this n is about 0.12 in the polarity rate, so a small reaction is not excluded.
